hook: Serial 153 from FBI Headquarters case file 62-HQ-83894 is an image-only document — a photograph or scanned page with no machine-readable text — filed within the Bureau's primary flying disc investigative record spanning June 1947 to July 1968.
why_it_matters: The 62-HQ-83894 case file is the FBI's central repository for UFO/flying disc reporting across more than two decades of the early Cold War period, and Serial 153 represents one discrete item within that accumulation. The PURSUE release version of this file is notable because it includes newly declassified pages and fewer redactions than the publicly available FBI Vault version, meaning this serial may contain content previously withheld. As an image document, its specific contribution to the record — whether photograph, handwritten memo, press clipping, or form — cannot be determined without visual inspection.
key_findings: The document is image-only with no extractable text, indicating it is either a photograph, a handwritten record, or a scanned page that was not OCR-processed.
It is filed as Serial 153 in case 62-HQ-83894, placing it late in the sequential accumulation of this multi-decade FBI headquarters file.
The parent case file is described as containing photographic evidence from Oak Ridge, TN — a nuclear research facility — suggesting this serial could relate to nuclear-site UAP observations.
The parent file also encompasses technical proposals on propulsion systems, eyewitness testimonies, and media coverage, any of which this serial could represent.
This version of the file originates from the PURSUE release on war.gov and is described as more complete than the FBI Vault version, with only minor redactions.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The parent case file overlaps temporally and topically with Project Blue Book (1952–1969), and FBI HQ files from this era frequently cross-reference Air Force investigative findings on flying disc reports.
The manifest explicitly cites photographic evidence from Oak Ridge, TN, an Atomic Energy Commission facility, directly linking this case file to nuclear-site UAP documentation.
Oak Ridge National Laboratory is one of the named sites associated with photographic evidence in this case file, making ORNL a direct institutional connection.

FBI headquarters files from 1947–1968 on flying discs routinely involved coordination with Wright-Patterson's Air Technical Intelligence Center, though no direct reference appears in this serial's metadata.
